steps.title: Cut the 2020 Profiles To
steps.text:
Cut four 340 mm 2020 alumunium profiles. Currently we need two but rest two will be needed in future

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Base%20Aluminium%20Profile%20340%20mm.f3d

tools.name: mitre saw is better but Hack saw will be fine too.

steps.title: Connect Three Way Corner Bracket
steps.text:
Connect The Three Way Corner Bracket in the both end of the two 340 mm alumunium profile. Use the screws given with the corner bracket for this application. 

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Three%20Way%20Corner%20Bracket.f3d

steps.title: Cut Two
steps.text:
Cut four 310 mm 2020 profiles, and join two with the rest of already cut and attached corner bracket to create a rectangle

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Base%20Aluminium%20Profile%20310%20mm.f3d
Now the Lower part of robot base is complete

Cut the 3mm Acreylic sheet using laser cutter. the dxf file can be found here. 

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Lower%20Board.dxf

3D Print the part Lower Board Support 1 and Lower Board Support 2 and then place them on top of acreylic. These board supper as additional support for the lower acrylic board so that it doesn't get scrached or damaged during heavy movement. 

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Lower%20Board%20Support%201.stl

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Lower%20Board%20Support%202.stl

Now 3d print the four feet for the base, they are saved as feet.stl  and then allign them and connect using M5 Countersunk Screws

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Feet.stl

Now cut four 118 mm 2020 alumunium profiles and then join them on the extruded part of the three way corner bracket and use hex key to join them

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Base%20Aluminium%20Profile%20118%20mm.f3d

now we will build the computing part that will be inside the base of the robot. so here we are using a full itx computer that is why we are following these steps, but your thing may vary if you use different compute like nvidia jetson or intel nuc. 

so for the itx pc inside robot base we first 3d print the power supply holder and then join it to one corner as shown. make sure that the power inlet of the psu faces the 340 mm alumunium profiles

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Power%20Supply%20Holder%20That%20Connects%20with%20Aluminium%20Profile.f3d

Now Place the PSU inside the 3d Printed Power Supply Holder, In this version we used CORSAIR CX Series CX650 650W 80 Plus Bronze but you can use any as long as they have the same dimension and uses non moduler connections. 

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/EL90045--STD--ATX%20Power%20Supply%20v1.f3d

parts.name: Power Supply Unit - CORSAIR CX Series CX650 650W 80 Plus Bronze

tools.name: Sccessories came With the Poewr Supply Unit Box

steps.text:
Now Print  PSU Exhust Air Guide and connect it with the the psu exhust holes side, this will make sure that the exhust of the psu doesn't come back or recirculate inside the robot base. Use single countersunk screws and drop in t nut to set it up with the alumunium profiles. 

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/PSU%20Exhust%20Air%20Guide.f3d

now 3d print the Mesh Protecting Part and use tape or small amount of glue to place it on top of Power Supply Inlet as it will prevent small stuff from entering the PSU During develpment of the robot. 

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Mesh%20Protecting%20Part.f3d
Next We Will Setup the Motherboard

3D Print theMotherboardd Base and then isnert m3 inserts in the four mouting holes for the motherboard. and then connect it to 340 mm profile. also keep the spacing as showin in the image (adding screenshots for this)

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Motherboard%20Base.f3d

Now 3d print the motherboard support left and motherboard support right. just join them with the motherboard base using m5 countersunk screws and nut (or you can just use m5 inserts, all of these will work) keep the top of them free as they will be connected later. 

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Motherboard%20Support%20Left.f3d

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Motherboard%20Support%20Right.f3d
now place the itx motherboard which already have cpu cooler and cooling fan. make sure to use a low profile cooling fan so that it fits inside the base

now 3d print the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/120mm%20Cooling%20Fan%20Gurd%20Mainly%20for%20CPU%20Cooler%20Fans.f3d so and it should just snap fit on the cooler fan of the motherboard.
now our motherboard is complete it is time for the cpu

3d print the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/GPU%20Holder%20Main.f3d and fill two small holes with m3 inserts and larger holes with m5 inserts, in the lower part place the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Cooler%20Master%20PCIe%204.0%20x16%20300mm%20Riser%20Cable.f3d and screww that in.

now 3d print the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/GPU%20Holder%20Mounting%20Parts.f3d and there will be four hole total, so in the center two holes conenct them with the gpu mounting bracket. the wedge on the ed printed parts should match with the gput bracket. 

But make sure to actually use a lowe profile gpu with the small form factor gpu bracket.

Once the GPU Holder Additional Support and the gpu mounting bracket is connected, insert the gput into the pcie slot and make sure it connects peroperly. the outer side of the GPU Holder Additional Support.f3d should match properly with the GPU Holder Main.f3d werhere we already put m5 inserts, now use m5 screws to actually connect them rigidly after

now 3d print the gpu holder additional suppert to make sure the gput doesn't get loose while transporting, it makes the gpu in the place. 

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/GPU%20Holder%20Additional%20Support.f3d

Now place the entire set up we just created for gpu mounting side and place it in the robot bas e and using the counte sunk m5 screws connect it with the 310 mm alumunium profiles. (need to add image showing the dimentions and tolerance)

now let's create the cooling fan setup. here we usind a single 120mm cooling fan https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/120mm_fan_asm%20v1.f3d and a custom 3d printed mount https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Fan%20Mount%20With%20Aluminium%20Profile.f3d to connect it with the alumunium profile. right now it uses m5 countersunk screws to connect with the 310 mm profiles. just screw the lower one as we still didn't set up the top 310 mm profiels yet.

now 3d print the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/120mm%20Fan%20Inlet%20Air%20Guide.f3d and place it in front of the fan so that fan doesn't scuk the same air from inside the robot base. the fan is set as pull in cool air setup. use 2 m5 countersunk screws and drop in nut to connect it with alumunium profiles.

now connect the other two 310mm profile and two 340 mm profile and theree way corner connector to form a rectangle again and place it on to p of the existing setup to complete the box of the lower part. 

make sure to connect the 2 screws that we left in the motherboard support arm with this newly added profiles. do the same for that one screw holes that left out earlier in the cooling fan 3d printed support.

now 3d print the power menu connector top part and there insert a m5 inserts and also 3d print the pwoer menu connector bottom part. 

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Power%20Menu%20Connector%20Top%20Part.f3d
https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Power%20Menu%20Connector%20Lower%20Part.f3d

now insert the device that holds the power button for p along with audio in out and couple of use connector. here we aure using the one pulled from DeepCool CH170 Digital Mini Tower, but you can any but you have to make the cusstom part for that. 

now place the thing from DeepCool CH170 Digital Mini Tower into the top part you just printed and then use the bottom part to secure it.
then connect the entire assembly with the top 340 mm alumunium profile (adding images for tolerance) using m5 countersunck screws and drop in nuts

now 3d print the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Motherboard%20Backplate.f3d which sits on top of the motherboard backplate and keeps proper air outlet so that eat can get out of that. 

secure it with two m5 countersunk and drop in t nut.
now wire up everything inside the robot base connect the gpu cpu and psue as from next on we will be continuein gto put the outside pannels of the robot base.
laser cut the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Right%20Board%20(Motherboard%20IO%20Side).dxf and then there you will see a cutout for the gx 16 connector.

now 3d print the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/GX%2016%20Holder.f3d which will hold the male side of the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/GX%2016-3%20Male.f3d gx 16 connector. secure it using nuts. then using m5 any screws and m5 nuts connect it with the acrylic pannel.

now its time to connect the firsst pannel. so now 3d print the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Screw%20Support%20for%20Board%20Small.f3d and print two of them and place it on top of borad and using foru countersunk screws and four drop in t nut secure the board withe alumunium profile skeleton. 

after that put the 3d printed gpu backplate https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Updated%20GPU%20Backplate%20v1.f3d there using the same m5 countersunk screws and m5 nuts

another thing is not that make sure to connect the wires between the gx16 connector because there will be a power line here thorugh an emergancy switch we will put later. 

when the gx 16 and gput mount si set then  like before use the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Screw%20Support%20for%20Board%20Small.f3d to connect it with the alumunium profiles using drop in t nut and m5 countersunk screws.

then laser cut the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Back%20Board.dxf and https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Front%20Board.dxf and then use the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Screw%20Support%20for%20Board%20Large.f3d to connect

now laser cut the left board https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Left%20Board.dxf and ed print the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/AC%20Power%20Enter%20Hole.f3d and press fit with the acreylic board. so here two cables will enter, one that will provide power to pc and the other one that will go through th eemergancy stop switch (which we will be installing later) to the female connector, so keep proper cable as need them in future.

now connect the last side which is front board https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Front%20Board.dxf and use the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Screw%20Support%20for%20Board%20Small.f3d and  four m5 countersunk screw and drop in t nut to attach this with ethe alumunium profiles.

now cut two more 310mm 2020 proofiles (https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Base%20Aluminium%20Profile%20310%20mm.f3d) and place them as shown in the animation/video and connect them using the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Corner%20Bracket.f3d and m5 screws and drop in t nut. 

(need to add tolerance image here)

now cut two more 218mm 2020 proofiles (https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Base%20Aluminium%20Profile%20218%20mm.f3d) and place them as shown in the animation/video and connect them using the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Corner%20Bracket.f3d and m5 screws and drop in t nut. 

(need to add tolerance image here)

3d print and place the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Protector%20for%20PC%20Components.f3d using the m5 screw and drop in nut. it have a lot of hoes so that it is easier for wire management.

laser cut the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Top%20Board.dxf and place it. make sure the square hole close to the gpu and cooling fan side as in that squre there will be cable mounting for emergancy shutoff switch where the cable needs re routing.

now 3d print https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Top%20Board%20Screw%20Support.f3d and put them on top of the top board and using drop in t nut and m5 counter sunk screws they will be connected with the alumunium profiles. 

also 3d print the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Emergency%20Switch%20Holder.f3d and put the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/AB6-A%20Emergency%20Switch.f3d there. solder the wires. the wire should be look like this, 220v ac cable one will enter in the power supply unit. create another 220v ac cable and socket that will enter throgh the power supply unit (ac power enter hole) and then go to the gx 16 connector through this emergancy switch. do not forget to use shrinking tube after soldering.

noe 3d print four https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Updated%20Main%20Body%20Lifter%20Support.f3d and place them in each corner of the shown (inside the top plate) and use countersunk screws and drop in nut to attach them securely.
now 3d print a single piece of the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Lazy%20Susan%20Bearing%20Holder%20with%20Servo%20Motor.f3d

in the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Lazy%20Susan%20Bearing%20Holder%20with%20Servo%20Motor.f3d you can fit a hiwonder htd 85h (with the circular shaft) and fit it in the bearing holder and at the bottom of the servo you will find six screws to secure the servo motor with the 3d printed parts.

then 3d print the hip driver gear https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Hip%20Driver%20Gear.f3d at around 60 percent infill and use screws given with htd 85 motor to connect it with the servo shaft.
then 3d print the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Lazy%20Susan%20Bearing%20Holder%20Without%20Motor.f3d

now put the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/25MM%20Nearly10%20Inch%20Rotating%20Table%20Bearing%20Lazy%20Suzan%20Bearing.f3d and you can clearly see the two parts we just 3d printed ligning up properly with the outer end of the bearing. now use a long screw to connect them. at the end of those two 3d printed parts you will see the slot for drop in t nut which allows you to screw the top part of the robot (from hip to head) individually. so any time you can just remove the top part of the robot and put it in the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Robot%20Temporary%20Base%20During%20Transportation.f3d and you are good to go. 

if wanna connect the robot permanently with the base you have to place this in the alumunium profile alongside those main body lifter and then you use tnut and m5 screws to permanently connect the robot with the base.

now put the entire setup we build including the bearing and the holder and servo motor setup in the slot in the alumunium profile (not permanent just as a temperary solution as we have to put a lot of screws there)

next place these things in order and make sure to align their forur holes currectly 

first goes 3d printed at more than 60 percent infill https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Inner%20Driven%20Gear%20of%20Hip.f3d

then goes 3d printed https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Mesh%20Protecting%20Part.f3d

then goes 3d printed https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Core%20Support.f3d

and when all these are put together use m5 screws from top and m5 hex nuts to bottom to connect all four of these layers securely.

now comes main four core profiles of the robot that will support the entire robot. 

343 mm profiles will be in the front side of the robot, https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Croe%20Profile%20Front%20Right.f3d and https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Croe%20Profile%20Front%20Left.f3d

then comes 393 mm 2020 alumunium profiles that will go at the back side, 

https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Croe%20Profile%20Back%20Left.f3d
and
https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Croe%20Profile%20Back%20Right.f3d

then use necessary screws and drop in nuts to hold these peorpfiles in place. notice there are are redundancy holes there, you do not need to use the inner four screws, you can just use m5 countersunk screws four that are on the outside to hold these profiles in place.

after the core propleis are set here comes the power supply unit. 

here we aure using a 12v 10a smps standard size for our application, this power suppply will mainly power the servo motors of the robot. 

so first connect the input and output cables of the smps, make a relatively long cable for the smps as the ac input cable will be connected to a gx 16 female cable that will go outside of the cable to connect to that female gx 16 cable in the robot base. and a short wire for the smps output as the motor driver will sit just on top of the power supply assembly. 

so first connect the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/12V%20SMPS%20Holder%20Lower%20Part.f3d at the lower side of smps (from where the cable is going out), the psu have mounting holes and use them. but they are m3 screws so keep that in the mind. also sometimes instead of screw holes they have mouting slots where you can use m3 screws and m3 hex nut to mount them. 

then mount the top part https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/12V%20SMPS%20Holder%20Upper%20Part.f3d with the sps too. 

now move the whole assembly at the back side of the robot (i need to include the tolerances image here), and use m5 countersunk and drop in nuts to attach the screws with the alumunium profiles. note that back side means the larger alumunium profiles and top front side means the smaller alon umunium profiles. 


put the Hiwonder BusLinker V3.0 Servo Debugging Board on top of the upper mouting part (there you will see holes ) suing double sided tape.

now 3d print these components at atleast 40 percent infill. https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Left%20Lower%20Generated%20Connector.f3d
https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Right%20Lower%20Generated%20Connector.f3d

after printing them you will see some hex slots there where you have to put m5 hex nut there so that screws can hold in there. we suggest after placing the hex nut  use some super glue so that they remain fix in their position. 

now attach these to components to the coreprofiles one in the left and one in the right and connect them using m5screws and drop in t nut. 

(i need to include the tolerance image here)

now its time to connect the display. this mount was made for the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/ViewSonic%20TD1655%20Simplified%20Model.f3d. 

the mount is made in a way so that it is easily replacable by small amount of twik. 

so you have to 3d print https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Display%20Connector%20with%20Core%20Profiles%20-%20Lower.f3d and https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Display%20Connector%20with%20Core%20Profiles%20-%20Upper.f3d

then attach the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/ViewSonic%20TD1655%20Display%20Holder.f3d with this. so if want to change display or use other type of display you have to create https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/ViewSonic%20TD1655%20Display%20Holder.f3d part from the scrats and then connect with other two using m5 countersunbnk screws.

finally once all is insert this entire display holder assembly into core profiles from the top (not that you have remove the power supply and its assembly for thsi part)

then use necessary screws to connect the foure side to the main core profiles using necessary screws. here we used regular flat head m5 screws with drop in t nut.

next there is a small part called have to be 3d printed and placed in the back two profiles https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Wire%20Guide%20-%20Small%20Version.f3d

this is just asmall part with a lot of holes so that it makes cable management easy and we cna just use couple of zip ties for easy cable routing.

now 3d print these components at atleast 40 percent infill. 
https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Left%20Upper%20Generated%20Connector.f3d
https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Right%20Upper%20Generated%20Connector.f3d

after printing them you will see some hex slots there where you have to put m5 hex nut there so that screws can hold in there. we suggest after placing the hex nut  use some super glue so that they remain fix in their position. 

now attach these to components to the coreprofiles one in the left and one in the right and connect them using m5screws and drop in t nut. 

(i need to include the tolerance image here)

next setup the hiwonder hx 35hm with its circular horn and 3d print the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Neck%20Tilt%20Gear%20Driver.f3d

and use screws to mount it with the horn of the servos.

once the driver gear is set with the servo, put the servo in the slots. 

and there are screw holes at the bottom so use those screws to mount the servos securely.

next we have to pu the bearing which is 6007 sealed bearing and then we have to print 60 percent infill https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Support%20for%20Neck%20Pan%20Gear%20Driven.f3d, and 60 percent infill https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Neck%20Pan%20Gear%20Driven.f3d and finally printing the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Neck%20Pan%20and%20Tilt%20Part%20Connection.f3d at 40 percent infill. 

once they are put properly and make sure the connection is perop then four very long scres will be mounted from top of https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Neck%20Pan%20and%20Tilt%20Part%20Connection.f3d and cnnect all these 3d printed parts together. here no drp in nut needed, only the screw thread holds them together. 

here the snugfit between the bearing 6007 and other is importatn ans the entire head will be supported using this friction fit. 

also at the center of the bearing kyou will find a hole that will be used to transfer a single servo cable (we will see that in future)

next take another https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Hiwonder%20HX-35HM.f3d along with the circular horn https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/HX-35HM%20Horn%20Connector.f3d and connect it with the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Neck%20Tilt%20Gear%20Driver.f3d using proper screws.

next put the motor and gear we just assembled inside the motor slot of the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Neck%20Pan%20and%20Tilt%20Part%20Connection.f3d and use screws to secure it ptoperly. 

now connect all these servos with the buslinker using cables.

now put two https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Bearing%206804-2RS%20(20x32x7).f3d  at two ends of the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Neck%20Pan%20and%20Tilt%20Part%20Connection.f3d

Then put the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Neck%20Tilt%20Left%20Head%20Joint.f3d  in the left side bearing (left on robot persperctive). 
and attach the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Neck%20Tilt%20Gear%20Driven.f3d with the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Bearing%206804-2RS%20(20x32x7).f3d using m5 flat head screws long and m5 hex (you will see there are slots for hex screws to go in)
in th eother side put the https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Neck%20Tilt%20Right%20Head%20Joint.f3d with the bearing (right from the robots perspective).

Tehn use flat head m5 screws and m5 hex nut to connect two end using 3d printed 60 percent infill https://github.com/tanvir-a0/CogniCare-Assembly-Documentation-2/blob/main/Left%20Right%20Head%20Joint%20Connector.f3d and notice that there are spots for 6 screws, but connecting 4 will be enought. the left side screw and nuts may be treacky as there is spaces ary very tight.
